version.changelog: 首次发布 - OpenClaw Gateway 重启性能分析工具

llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says (reads OpenClaw logs, stops/starts the gateway, and generates a report), but there are mismatches between its metadata/README and the actual script (missing Windows PS1, undeclared required binaries) and it will stop/start a running gateway and read user log files — so review and caution are warranted before running it on production systems.

dimensions.detail: The declared purpose (profile gateway restart) matches the included Bash script's behavior: it locates OpenClaw logs, starts the gateway, monitors startup log lines and produces reports. However the skill metadata declares no required binaries/env but the script clearly expects an 'openclaw' CLI and utilities like dd, stat, date and bc. Also SKILL.md advertises a Windows PowerShell script (gateway-profile.ps1) but no .ps1 file is present in the package — an inconsistency between claimed multi-platform support and supplied files.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running the included script which (correctly) reads logs and generates HTML/text reports. The instructions call out starting/stopping the gateway — that is within the profiling scope, but it is an intrusive action (it stops a live service). SKILL.md references a Windows script that is missing from the files; the Linux invocation is present and consistent with the script.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec — instruction-only with a bundled shell script. No downloads or third-party installers are executed by the skill itself, which minimizes installation risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or binaries, yet the script needs the 'openclaw' command and Unix utilities (stat, dd, date, bc). It reads user log files under ~/.openclaw/logs and /tmp and writes reports there — access to those files is proportionate to profiling but should be explicit. The generated HTML references Chart.js via https://cdn.jsdelivr.net, so opening the report will cause the browser to fetch remote JS from a CDN (not the script itself performing network exfiltration, but remote content is loaded when the user opens the HTML). No credentials are requested or read.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always:true and does not request persistent privileges. It does perform transient, potentially privileged actions (stopping/starting the gateway), but it doesn't install persistent agents or modify other skills' configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to implement a legitimate restart profiler, but there are a few issues to consider before installing or running it:

- Review the script contents manually (scripts/gateway-profile.sh) before running. It will stop and start the OpenClaw gateway (openclaw gateway stop/start), which can disrupt production traffic.
- Make sure the host has the expected 'openclaw' CLI and Unix utilities (dd, stat, date, bc). The package metadata did not list these requirements — verify them yourself.
- The SKILL.md promises a Windows PowerShell script (gateway-profile.ps1) but that file is not included; if you need Windows support, obtain/verify the PS1 implementation first.
- The script reads logs under ~/.openclaw/logs and /tmp and writes HTML/text reports there; ensure you are comfortable with it accessing those files and have backups if needed.
- The generated HTML references Chart.js from jsDelivr; opening the report will fetch remote resources in your browser. If this is a concern, host Chart.js locally or inspect the HTML before opening.
- Run this tool first in a staging/non-production environment and with an account that can be safely used to stop/start services. If you lack confidence in the script, ask the author for the missing Windows script and an explicit list of required binaries and permissions.
